import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing for Visualization ---
# Drop rows with missing 'Income' values, as they are crucial for this visualization
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Calculate total spending across all product categories
spending_columns = [col for col in df.columns if col.startswith('Mnt')]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[spending_columns].sum(axis=1)

# --- Visualization ---
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 9)) # Adjust figure size for better readability

# Create a scatter plot to visualize Total Spending vs. Income,
# colored by Education level to reveal potential segmentation patterns.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Education',
    palette='viridis', # Choose a color palette
    alpha=0.7,         # Add transparency to handle potential overplotting
    s=70,              # Adjust marker size
    edgecolor='w',     # Add white edge to markers for better separation
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Customer Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Annual Income', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending (USD)', fontsize=14)

# Improve legend placement and title
plt.legend(title='Education Level', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11',
           bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Ensure all elements fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
